_readme: What the Items tab can make. A kind is one sort of thing (a cutlass, boots, a helmet): `noun` is how the pictures' prompts name it, `hint` describes it when the description is empty, `pose` picks how its main picture is staged (see "poses"), `size_m` is the longest side of the finished model in metres (the 3D model is scaled to it), `pivot` is where the model's origin goes (base = the middle of the bottom, centre, grip = a handle: `grip_at` is how far up the model the hand holds it, 0 = the bottom, 1 = the top) and `attach` names the bone of the characters' skeleton (the animation library's names) it is usually parented to. `front` says which side of the thing counts as its front, for the four views. Measured 2026-10-02 with a cutlass, boots and a helmet: the main picture from Z-Image Turbo, the four views from Qwen-Image-Edit 2511 and the shape from Trellis2 (about five minutes each, npcgen/items.py). Garments are staged on an invisible mannequin and are the least tested kind. `high` (on a family, or a kind that says otherwise) is whether two more pictures from 45 degrees above, in front and behind, are drawn for the paint: the four level views never see the top of a helmet, a crate or a boot's opening, which came out patchy; long thin things stood up or turned upside down in them, so weapons and garments have none. A kind with a `front` (boots, helmets, bags, garments) has its two side views told which way the front points (left, right of the picture): without it the pair of boots came back with the same side view twice (toes to the right in both) and the paint matched them to the shape at 0.5, with it 0.90. Told the same, a cutlass came back lying on its side with the tip pointing left, so things that stand up (swords, axes, spears, bows) have no front. A family with a `maker` is not drawn: its things are built from a recipe (glasses: npcgen/glasses.py, fitted clothes: npcgen/clothing.py) and its kinds say where the model's origin is (`bridge`: between the eyes; `floor`: the floor between the feet of the body the clothes are made for).

stylised.label: Stylised game asset
stylised.phrase: stylised 3D game asset, clean sculpted forms, hand-painted textures, well-defined materials, soft global illumination

painted.label: Hand-painted fantasy
painted.phrase: hand-painted fantasy game asset, painterly textures, bold readable shapes, soft lighting

voxel.label: Voxel art
voxel.phrase: voxel art object built from visible cube-shaped blocks, blocky low-resolution 3D form, flat lit faces, sharp cube edges, bright saturated colors

upright.hero: standing upright on its end, the whole length in frame

pair.hero: a matching pair standing side by side on the ground

single.hero: a single one resting on the ground

side.hero: shown in profile from the side, the whole length in frame

ghost.hero: shown on an invisible mannequin (a ghost mannequin product photo): it holds its shape as if worn by an invisible person, the inside of the neck and sleeves visible, no person, no face, no hands
ghost.negative: person, model, face, hands, skin, legs, mannequin head, hanger

garment.label: Garments

coat.hint: a long wool coat with buttons and a collar
coat.front: the button side is the front

cloak.label: Cloak

clothing.label: Fitted clothes
clothing.blurb: A sleeveless shirt, fitted trousers, a knee-length skirt, a sleeveless dress, an open jacket or a bib apron, built from measurements (colour, looseness, length, cloth) and fitted to a designed body, so they follow every animation. A jacket or an apron goes over a shirt and trousers, a skirt is worn with a shirt instead of trousers and a dress is worn on its own instead of both: those are the only ways the Body Designer has checked them. Not drawn from a picture: the pattern is ready at once, and trying one on a character takes about half a minute. Only a body made by the Body Designer can wear them.

shirt.hint: a plain sleeveless shirt in a muted teal
shirt.front: the lower neckline is the front

views.side_left: seen straight from its left side (turned 90 degrees)
views.side_right: seen straight from its right side (turned 90 degrees)

views_high.front_high: seen from the front and above, from a high angle of 45 degrees looking down on it
views_high.back_high: seen from behind and above, from a high angle of 45 degrees looking down on it

views_facing.side_left: seen straight from the side, turned 90 degrees so that its front points to the left of the picture
views_facing.side_right: seen straight from the side, turned 90 degrees the other way so that its front points to the right of the picture

prompts.hero: {subject}, {pose}. Studio product shot of the single {thing}, three-quarter view, the whole {thing} in frame on a plain white background, soft even light, {look}
prompts.hero_negative: text, watermark, hands, person, mannequin, multiple objects, cropped, shadow on the floor, collage
prompts.view: Show the exact same {noun} again, {where}. Keep its shape, proportions, colours and materials exactly the same, the whole {thing} in frame, the same plain white background, no shadow, no person.
prompts.view_front: Show the exact same {noun} again.{front} It is {where}. Keep its shape, proportions, colours and materials exactly the same, the whole {thing} in frame, the same plain white background, no shadow, no person.
prompts.view_negative: text, watermark, hands, person, mannequin, multiple objects, cropped, shadow on the floor, collage
